#====================================================================================================
# START - Testing Protocol - DO NOT EDIT OR REMOVE THIS SECTION
#====================================================================================================

# THIS SECTION CONTAINS CRITICAL TESTING INSTRUCTIONS FOR BOTH AGENTS
# BOTH MAIN_AGENT AND TESTING_AGENT MUST PRESERVE THIS ENTIRE BLOCK

# Communication Protocol:
# If the `testing_agent` is available, main agent should delegate all testing tasks to it.
#
# You have access to a file called `test_result.md`. This file contains the complete testing state
# and history, and is the primary means of communication between main and the testing agent.
#
# Main and testing agents must follow this exact format to maintain testing data. 
# The testing data must be entered in yaml format Below is the data structure:
# 
## user_problem_statement: {problem_statement}
## backend:
##   - task: "Task name"
##     implemented: true
##     working: true  # or false or "NA"
##     file: "file_path.py"
##     stuck_count: 0
##     priority: "high"  # or "medium" or "low"
##     needs_retesting: false
##     status_history:
##         -working: true  # or false or "NA"
##         -agent: "main"  # or "testing" or "user"
##         -comment: "Detailed comment about status"
##
## frontend:
##   - task: "Task name"
##     implemented: true
##     working: true  # or false or "NA"
##     file: "file_path.js"
##     stuck_count: 0
##     priority: "high"  # or "medium" or "low"
##     needs_retesting: false
##     status_history:
##         -working: true  # or false or "NA"
##         -agent: "main"  # or "testing" or "user"
##         -comment: "Detailed comment about status"
##
## metadata:
##   created_by: "main_agent"
##   version: "1.0"
##   test_sequence: 0
##   run_ui: false
##
## test_plan:
##   current_focus:
##     - "Task name 1"
##     - "Task name 2"
##   stuck_tasks:
##     - "Task name with persistent issues"
##   test_all: false
##   test_priority: "high_first"  # or "sequential" or "stuck_first"
##
## agent_communication:
##     -agent: "main"  # or "testing" or "user"
##     -message: "Communication message between agents"

# Protocol Guidelines for Main agent
#
# 1. Update Test Result File Before Testing:
#    - Main agent must always update the `test_result.md` file before calling the testing agent
#    - Add implementation details to the status_history
#    - Set `needs_retesting` to true for tasks that need testing
#    - Update the `test_plan` section to guide testing priorities
#    - Add a message to `agent_communication` explaining what you've done
#
# 2. Incorporate User Feedback:
#    - When a user provides feedback that something is or isn't working, add this information to the relevant task's status_history
#    - Update the working status based on user feedback
#    - If a user reports an issue with a task that was marked as working, increment the stuck_count
#    - Whenever user reports issue in the app, if we have testing agent and task_result.md file so find the appropriate task for that and append in status_history of that task to contain the user concern and problem as well 
#
# 3. Track Stuck Tasks:
#    - Monitor which tasks have high stuck_count values or where you are fixing same issue again and again, analyze that when you read task_result.md
#    - For persistent issues, use websearch tool to find solutions
#    - Pay special attention to tasks in the stuck_tasks list
#    - When you fix an issue with a stuck task, don't reset the stuck_count until the testing agent confirms it's working
#
# 4. Provide Context to Testing Agent:
#    - When calling the testing agent, provide clear instructions about:
#      - Which tasks need testing (reference the test_plan)
#      - Any authentication details or configuration needed
#      - Specific test scenarios to focus on
#      - Any known issues or edge cases to verify
#
# 5. Call the testing agent with specific instructions referring to test_result.md
#
# IMPORTANT: Main agent must ALWAYS update test_result.md BEFORE calling the testing agent, as it relies on this file to understand what to test next.

#====================================================================================================
# END - Testing Protocol - DO NOT EDIT OR REMOVE THIS SECTION
#====================================================================================================



#====================================================================================================
# Testing Data - Main Agent and testing sub agent both should log testing data below this section
#====================================================================================================

frontend:
  - task: "Portfolio (Our Work) last card sticky stacking fix"
    implemented: true
    working: true
    file: "/app/frontend/src/sections/PortfolioSection.jsx"
    stuck_count: 0
    priority: "high"
    needs_retesting: false
    status_history:
        - working: "NA"
          agent: "main"
          comment: "USER REGRESSION #2: last card 'goes up halfway, comes back down, then goes ALONE (not with the other cards) as scrolling continues'. TRAJECTORY TRACE revealed the real root cause: each card had a trailing mb-[54vh] margin, and a sticky element with a bottom margin UNSTICKS EARLY (the margin reserves space at the bottom of its containing block). So case-study-4 unstuck/left (~scrollY 4846, top -76) BEFORE case-study-5 reached its stacked top (226 at ~scrollY 5086) — the cards never coexisted stuck, so the last card arrived alone. This was actually a conveyor, not an accumulating deck. STRUCTURAL FIX: removed all per-card margins; spacing between cards is now provided by SEPARATE spacer siblings (Fragment) between the cards, plus a final hold spacer. With no trailing margin, every card stays stuck until the container's true end, so cards ACCUMULATE into a real deck and RELEASE TOGETHER. gapVh = isMobile?22:50, finalHoldVh = isMobile?26:30. VERIFIED via trajectory trace (Lenis-settle on desktop): DESKTOP at scrollY 4898 c2=148,c3=174,c4=200,c5=226 all stuck simultaneously (deck), hold, then all converge (5228 all=88) and release together. agent_communication:
    - agent: "main"
      message: "NEW BACKEND (agency management) to test. Admin password '180406kon' (POST /api/admin/login -> token, header X-Admin-Token). All new routes require admin auth. Test CRUD + relations: (A) CLIENTS: POST /api/admin/clients {name,...} creates; GET /api/admin/clients lists; PATCH /api/admin/clients/{id} updates; DELETE /api/admin/clients/{id}. (B) PROJECTS: POST /api/admin/projects {name, client_id?, type, status, budget, deadline, staging_url, live_url, login_notes,...}; GET list; PATCH {status} moves pipeline; DELETE (should also delete its tasks). (C) TASKS: POST /api/admin/tasks {project_id,title}; GET /api/admin/tasks?project_id=...; PATCH {done:true}; DELETE. Verify deleting a project cascades and removes its tasks. (D) INVOICES: POST /api/admin/invoices {client_id?,project_id?,amount,amount_paid,status,due_date,...}; verify status auto-normalizes (amount_paid=0->Unpaid, 0<paid<amount->Partial, paid>=amount->Paid) unless status explicitly 'Paid'; GET list; PATCH; DELETE. (E) OVERVIEW: GET /api/admin/overview returns {clients_total, active_projects, projects_total, revenue_this_month, total_collected, outstanding, invoices_total, upcoming_deadlines[], unpaid_invoices[]}; create a client+project(with deadline)+invoice(partial) and confirm counts/aggregates reflect them (active_projects counts non-'Ολοκληρωμένο'; outstanding = sum(amount-amount_paid) for non-Paid). (F) CONVERT: create a contact via POST /api/contact then POST /api/admin/clients/from-lead/{contact_id} -> creates client (name=company or name), and the contact status becomes 'Converted'. Create a prospect via POST /api/admin/prospects/bulk then POST /api/admin/clients/from-prospect/{prospect_id} -> creates client and REMOVES the prospect. (G) auth: any admin route without token -> 401. Clean up test data at the end. Do NOT test frontend."

          comment: "USER BUG (mobile first visit): After the IntroOverlay scroll lock fix, user reported scroll STILL got stuck on first visit, just 'a bit further down the page'. ROOT CAUSE #2: In ChatDesktop.jsx (the interactive idea generator demo mockup in Hero section), the results panel div (data-testid='hero-ideas-results', line 166) had `overflow-y-auto overscroll-contain` applied unconditionally (all breakpoints). This div sits prominently in the middle of the hero content on mobile — right where a user's thumb naturally starts a scroll swipe.   - task: "Portfolio Section Last Card Stacking Bug Fix"
    implemented: true
    working: true
    file: "/app/frontend/src/sections/PortfolioSection.jsx"
    stuck_count: 0
    priority: "high"
    needs_retesting: false
    status_history:
        - working: "NA"
          agent: "main"
          comment: "USER BUG REPORT: On mobile (390x844), in the 'Our Work' / Portfolio section (#portfolio, 6 sticky-stacking case-study cards: data-testid='case-study-0' through 'case-study-5'), the LAST card ('Πλατφόρμα Αγγελιών Ακινήτων' / real estate) did not fully stack over the previous card — it stopped moving midway instead of completing its upward sticky travel like all the other cards do. ROOT CAUSE: Each card is a position: sticky element with a staggered top offset (peek/stack effect) and non-last cards get a large margin-bottom (mb-[16vh] mobile / mb-[54vh] desktop) which gives them 'dwell' time to stay stuck before the next card arrives. The LAST card had no card after it, and — critically, verified via direct browser testing — a sticky element's OWN trailing margin or padding does NOT give it any dwell/stuck room in the browser's sticky positioning algorithm; it only gets stuck dwell time from an actual DOM sibling that follows it within the same containing block. Since the last card had nothing after it, it never actually entered its 'stuck' state at all — it just slid straight through its target position without pausing, giving the appearance of 'stopping midway' / not completing the stack. FIX: Added an explicit trailing spacer <div aria-hidden style={height: ...} /> as a real sibling AFTER the last card inside the sticky-cards container (line 175). Previously tried margin-bottom on the card and padding-bottom on the container, both of which did NOT work — only a genuine sibling element works. This gives the last card real dwell/stuck room so it now properly sticks and fully stacks over the second-to-last card before smoothly continuing on to the CTA panel below. Needs verification on mobile viewport (390x844): (1) Scroll down through the 'Our Work' / Portfolio section (#portfolio), watching all 6 stacked case-study cards. (2) Confirm the LAST card (real estate / 'Πλατφόρμα Αγγελιών Ακινήτων') now behaves the SAME WAY as the earlier cards: it slides up, becomes pinned/sticky, and fully visually covers/stacks over the second-to-last card (leaving only the expected thin peek/sliver of the card behind it), rather than stopping partway or never appearing to 'stick'. (3) Confirm after the last card finishes its stack, scrolling continues smoothly into the CTA panel ('Θες κάτι παρόμοιο για την επιχείρησή σου;') with no big blank gap and no jump/glitch.
